title: JRE 2378 - Charlie Sheen
guestBio: Charlie Sheen is an actor best known for his leading roles in films such as "Platoon," "Wall Street," "Major League," and "Rooftop Killer," and television shows including "Spin City" (for which he won a Golden Globe Award) and "Two and a Half Men." His new book, "The Book of Sheen," is available now. He is featured in the Netflix documentary, "AKA Charlie Sheen," streaming now. Charlie has recently co-founded a new non-alcoholic beer brand called Wild AF, which will be available in October. Born Carlos Estevez, Sheen lives in Malibu, CA, where he grew up.

recap:
Joe sits down with Charlie Sheen in this wide-ranging conversation that covers the actor's legendary career and his current projects. They dive into his iconic roles that defined 90s and 2000s entertainment, from military drama in Platoon to the greed-fueled Wall Street and the baseball comedy Major League that became a cultural touchstone. Charlie opens up about his time on Spin City, which earned him a Golden Globe, and his massive success on Two and a Half Men before his highly publicized exit from the show.

A major focus of the conversation is Charlie's new book 'The Book of Sheen,' which appears to be a reflective project where he shares his perspective on life, career, and personal growth. Joe and Charlie discuss the motivation behind writing it and what fans can expect. They also talk about his Netflix documentary 'AKA Charlie Sheen,' which gives viewers an intimate look at his life and journey through the entertainment industry.

Charlie brings up his latest business venture, a non-alcoholic beer brand called Wild AF that's set to launch in October. This represents an interesting pivot for someone who's had a complicated relationship with substance use, and Charlie seems enthusiastic about the product and what it represents. The conversation around this brand launch touches on his current mindset and priorities.

Throughout the episode, Charlie demonstrates a reflective quality, discussing his experiences in Hollywood, the pressures of fame, and how he's moved forward. The energy between Joe and Charlie is relaxed and genuine, allowing for both humor and more serious moments about personal growth and redemption.
